summary.text: Lori Goss-Reaves is a Republican state representative who represents Indiana House District 31, has served since 2023, and is on the ballot for re-election on November 3, 2026. She is a social work professor who was appointed to the seat by the Republican Party of Indiana.

paragraphs.text: Lori Goss-Reaves earned a bachelor's degree from Ball State University, a graduate degree in social work from Indiana University-Purdue University Indianapolis, and a doctorate in social work from Capella University.
Her career experience includes working as a professor of social work and director of field placement at Indiana Wesleyan University.
The Republican Party of Indiana appointed Goss-Reaves to District 31 on May 31, 2023, to replace Ann Vermilion.
She advanced from the Republican primary on May 5, 2026, and in the November 3, 2026 general election she faces Democrat Katie Robins.
For 2025-2026, she was assigned to the Family, Children and Human Affairs, Insurance (as vice chair) and Public Health committees.
